source.title: Signed-Permutation Coordinate Transport for RMSNorm Transformers

page_placements.theme: Mapping and correspondence recovery depend on direction, geometry, anchors and optimization

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Refines the scope of coordinate mapping: it reports probe- and matching-rule-dependent alignment results, and argues that function-level information alone cannot define canonical coordinate transport between independently specified endpoints. It does not test convergence of representation distances with model scale.
record.gate_note: The paper measures signed-permutation coordinate recovery, transfers coordinate-indexed artifacts, and reports alignment stability under changes in probes and matching cost. These bear on V4 and V6, but it does not compare distances between representations as models scale or become more capable. Gauge-invariance checks, optimizer-state results, merging barriers, refusal ablation, and cited findings are not rows for the tested versions because they do not measure representation interchangeability or convergence as named by those versions.
record.test_reason: The paper uses activation-based coordinate matching as a tool. It reports its own method's accuracy against a gauge it imposes and records itself. Nearly every experiment applies a random signed permutation to one model, or to a shared base before fine-tuning, then scores recovery of that known map or of tools moved through it. The rows therefore compare the study's methods with one another: sign-marginalized vs signed-cost matching, transport vs endpoint, Bd vs Sd. They do not measure whether independently trained models' representations converge or are interchangeable. The only natural-alignment results are a stability score against a large-probe reference (Table 13) and one small 10M-parameter independent-seed merge-barrier run. Both are related constructs, not rates of convergence or interchangeability.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right, but the emphasis is off. The main conclusion is that RMSNorm transformers are coordinate-identifiable only up to signed permutation. Permutation-only alignment is therefore incomplete: sign-marginalized matching is required, and Sd transport destroys transferred LoRA, SAE and steering artifacts. Composing local gauges along same-base trajectories beats endpoint matching. Coordinate-indexed interpretability claims are reproducible only relative to an explicit gauge. The 'no canonical function-level transport' point is a supporting proposition, not the headline.
record.recipe_differences: Uses signed-permutation gauge recovery, coordinate transport, and artifact-transfer tests rather than comparing representation distances as in the cited convergence work; it tests coordinate identity and mapping, not scale-dependent representational convergence.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery depends on probe set and token budget, matching raw signed versus absolute correlations, endpoint versus composed local transport, training horizon, and whether signs are included.

fits_no_version.finding: Natural-alignment matching between Qwen2.5-1.5B and a same-architecture variant trained on different data. Agreement with a 36K-token reference rises from 5.7% at 39 tokens to 93.6% at 27K tokens. The sign-flip fraction falls from 47.3% to about 5%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-based coordinate matching between naturally differing same-architecture LLMs is probe-hungry: the recovered correspondence stabilizes only with roughly 10K–30K tokens.

fits_no_version.finding: Two 10M-parameter RMSNorm transformers trained on the same data from different seeds show about 50% sign mismatch. The merge barrier falls from 1.68 (unaligned) to 0.66 with permutation-only alignment and to 0.42 with signed alignment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Independently seeded RMSNorm networks are partly related by a signed permutation; sign-aware alignment reduces but does not remove the interpolation barrier.

fits_no_version.finding: Dropping signs when transporting coordinate-indexed artifacts under an exact gauge collapses them: SAE NMSE 0.004 vs 1.08, LoRA gain 99.7% vs −0.5%, refusal steering reversed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In RMSNorm transformers, coordinate correspondence requires signed permutations; permutation-only alignment is symmetry-incomplete.

record.problems: Most mapping experiments use an imposed, recorded gauge as ground truth and concern coordinate-indexed artifacts rather than representation-distance similarity. Natural cross-model alignment is primarily reported as stability against a large-probe reference, not ground-truth accuracy. The independent-seed merge example is small-scale; the paper does not test model capability scaling or modality differences.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted results not directly measuring representation mapping or alignment stability, including logit-invariance checks, optimizer-state trajectory comparisons, merge barriers, refusal ablation, and cited prior-work results. Table 4 pair-type breakdown was not separately extracted because its flattened layout does not unambiguously assign all displayed values to conditions; aggregate recovery and method comparisons are recorded from Table 17.

untested.parts: No scaling or capability sweep of cross-model alignment.
No vision-language paired-data alignment. ViT appears only in a gauge-invariance check.
No measure of shared features or subspaces across seeds. The only independent-seed run (10M parameters) reports sign mismatch and merge barriers.

No mapping between independently trained or differently architected models. All mapping results recover imposed gauges between functionally identical or same-base models. No stitching, relative representations or linear maps between distinct models.
No comparison of recurring features or circuits across distinct models. Gauge audits only show that coordinate names move under exact symmetries.
No similarity measure (CKA etc.) compared across choices for distinct models. No neighbour counts or OOD inputs.
No plateau or shared-data explanation tested.

missing.what: Independent-seed 10M RMSNorm merge: sign mismatch about 50%; barrier 1.68 / 0.66 / 0.42 (unaligned / Sd / Bd). This is the only natural independent-seed result and is closest to V3, though it measures merge barriers rather than feature overlap.

record.verdict_notes: The reader classed this as T5 testing V4 and V6, but nearly all results recover a gauge the authors imposed and recorded themselves. The models are either exact gauge-transformed copies or same-base fine-tunes carrying that imposed gauge. The rows are therefore method-vs-method performance, not evidence about convergence or interchangeability between independently trained models. No verdicts are given. The reader's V6 label on r11–r15 also cited rows tagged only V4.

versions.untested_parts: No scaling sweep relating representation alignment to model size or capability.
No paired image-caption or other vision-language representation alignment.
The small independent-seed experiment reports sign mismatch and merge barriers, not convergence of features or shared subspaces across seeds.

Tests signed-permutation coordinate transport and transfer of coordinate-indexed artifacts. Does not test stitching layers, relative representations, transport without paired activation probes, or broad interchangeability across different architectures or modalities.
No comparison of recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.
Tests probe-budget and matching-cost dependence for coordinate alignment. Does not compare distance-similarity measures such as CKA, vary neighbourhood counts, or test out-of-distribution inputs.
Does not test whether representation alignment plateaus or whether shared training data/objectives explain convergence rather than a common model of reality.

relation.reason: Activation matching is used to recover coordinate maps and transfer artifacts. Agreement with a large-probe matching reference does not establish shared representations, interchangeability with little loss, or convergence with scale.

tranche.reason: The study evaluates coordinate-recovery and artifact-transport methods, predominantly against imposed, recorded gauges. Table 13 evaluates matching stability rather than representation convergence. The natural independent-seed merge control reports alignment-method performance rather than directly establishing a claim version.

source_check.notes: Table 13 measures matched-index stability, not ground-truth accuracy or representation similarity. The paper also includes a natural independent-seed merge control, so its experiments should not all be described as imposed-gauge tests.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Recorded signed-permutation gauges and transported coordinate-indexed tools
reader_labels.reason: Recovery and transfer are strong with signed-permutation transport in the reported settings: TinyLlama recovery is 100% even at 22 tokens (r49–r54), sentiment transfer is 95.8% (r30), and SAE NMSE matches its reference at 0.004 (r34, r36).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Long-horizon or endpoint-based cross-run transport and FFN transfer
reader_labels.reason: Recovery and transfer are incomplete and vary by method, step count, model, and component; endpoint and some long-horizon FFN results are substantially below the fresh/reference target (r1–r10, r38–r48).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Omitting signs impairs transfer: SAE NMSE rises to 1.08, sentiment preservation is 17.2%, and refusal steering reverses (r31, r33, r35).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Natural-alignment probe budget and matching-cost choice
reader_labels.reason: Alignment agreement rises with probe count, and raw signed-correlation matching performs far worse than absolute-correlation matching on recorded signed gauges (r16–r22, r24–r29).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Probe budget in direct long-stride recovery
reader_labels.reason: Permutation recovery remains incomplete at 39–270 tokens but reaches 100% at the two larger tested probe budgets; the reported sign recovery remains 100% (r11–r15).
